subject: biology
title: Birth and Beyond
welcome_lead: Discover how a baby leaves the safety of the uterus and takes its first breath of air.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on childbirth basics and life after birth.
final_note: You now understand the basics of how a baby is born and starts its first days.

walkthroughs.body_html: At about 40 weeks the muscles of the uterus start strong contractions. These push the baby out through the vagina. This is called labour.
The newborn takes its first breath, switching to its own lungs. The umbilical cord is cut. Soon afterwards the placenta is delivered too.
The mother can feed the baby through breastfeeding. Milk contains everything a newborn needs. Babies sleep a lot and grow very quickly.

mcqs.q: Why are frameshift mutations usually more severe than point substitutions?
options: Insertions/deletions of a non-multiple of 3 shift the reading frame, changing every codon downstream of the mutation.
Frameshifts only change the codon at the site of the mutation, like a substitution.
PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.

options: PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.

PCR has just one stage — heating the DNA until it copies itself.
Denaturation (high temp, strands separate), annealing (lower temp, primers bind), extension (Taq polymerase synthesises new strands).
